channel.title: API Changelog
channel.description: Stay updated with API changes and version history

item.title: Filter historical fills by multiple market tickers
item.description: GET /historical/fills accepts up to 100 comma-separated market tickers in the ticker query parameter.
item.content:encoded: GET /historical/fills accepts up to 100 comma-separated market tickers in the ticker query parameter. A single ticker still works.

item.title: Breached exit-trigger prices get their own error codes
item.description: Exit-trigger writes reject a take profit or stop loss the mark has already passed by more than 2% with take_profit_already_breached or stop_loss_already_breached.
item.content:encoded: Margin exit-trigger writes reject a take_profit_price or stop_loss_price the current mark has already passed by more than 2% with 400 and error code take_profit_already_breached or stop_loss_already_breached. These were 400 responses whose code was not a stable identifier.

item.title: Weather point markets are described in the location's time zone
item.description: New weather point markets have their title, rules and local dates written in the time zone of the market's location, whatever timezone the POST /weather_point_markets request used. The max_window_days limit goes by the location's dates.
item.content:encoded:
A new weather point market is now described in the time zone of its location, which Kalshi determines from the coordinates. The timezone in POST /weather_point_markets still decides which span of time your date and hours mean, and the request body, the response and tickers are unchanged. What changes, for markets created from now on:

  • title and rules_primary, as returned by GET /markets and GET /events, give the window in the location's zone, whatever zone created the market. A request for 11pm to 3am in America/New_York at a point in Portland, Oregon used to produce a market reading in Eastern time, "from 11pm EST Thu, Nov 19 to 3am EST Fri, Nov 20, 2026"; it now reads "on Thu, Nov 19, 2026, 8pm–12am PST", and its rules "from 8pm to 12am PST (America/Los_Angeles) starting Thu, Nov 19, 2026". A market requested in its location's own zone reads as before.
  • Where GET /weather_point_markets/availability returns max_window_days: 1, a new market is refused with 409 weather_point_market_unavailable when its window crosses midnight at the location, and accepted when it doesn't, even if your request sets end_date. It no longer depends on the dates of the first request for the event, which replaces what the entry below says.
  • A window that crosses midnight at the location and is longer than 24 hours there returns 400 invalid_parameters, even when your request names it within one date of another zone.
  • A location whose time zone can't be determined returns 409 weather_point_market_unavailable.

Events that already exist keep their description, and a new threshold on one of them reads like the rest of that event. See On-Request Weather Markets.

item.title: Listener mode on KalshiRFQ sessions
item.description: A KalshiRFQ session that logs on with ListenerSession<20126>=Y also receives your account's execution reports.
item.content:encoded: KalshiRFQ sessions can now choose listener mode with ListenerSession<20126>=Y. The session keeps quoting and also receives your account's execution reports, including the fills of your accepted quotes. See Listener Sessions.

item.title: Weather point markets can cross midnight
item.description: POST /weather_point_markets takes an optional end_date, the day after date, for a window that runs from one local day into the next, up to 24 hours long. GET /weather_point_markets/availability returns max_window_days and max_window_hours.
item.content:encoded:
A weather point market's window can now run from one local day into the next, for example 11pm to 3am:

  • POST /weather_point_markets takes an optional end_date. Left out, or equal to date, the request means what it did before. Set to the day after date, the window runs from start_hour on date to end_hour on end_date. Such a window is at most 24 hours long, so end_hour must not be after start_hour; a longer window, or any other end_date, returns 400 invalid_parameters.
  • end_hour no longer has to be after start_hour when end_date is the day after date. For a window on one day it still must be.
  • GET /weather_point_markets/availability returns max_window_days (2 where a window may cross midnight, otherwise 1) and max_window_hours (the longest such window, 24). Where max_window_days is 1, a new market whose window is stored across two local dates returns 409 weather_point_market_unavailable. A market stores the dates of the first request for its variable, point and window, normally your own. When that event already exists, its dates decide: a one-date request from another time zone for an event stored across midnight returns the 409, and a request with end_date for an event stored on one date succeeds. Markets that already exist are returned either way.

Tickers keep their shape: the window is still its UTC start and its length in hours, so 11pm November 23 to 3am November 24 in New York is …-26NOV2404Z-4H-…. Existing markets and requests without end_date are unchanged. See On-Request Weather Markets.

item.title: Weather point markets use your exact coordinates
item.description: POST /weather_point_markets no longer snaps the location to the center of its weather grid cell. The market's location is the requested coordinates rounded to three decimal places, so two points in the same grid cell are now two markets.
item.content:encoded:
POST /weather_point_markets no longer snaps the location to the center of the NOAA MRMS grid cell containing it. The market's location is now the requested latitude and longitude rounded to three decimal places (about 100 m), and the response's latitude and longitude return that point.

  • Requests share a market only when their coordinates agree to three decimal places. Two points in the same grid cell used to resolve to one market and now resolve to two.
  • A rounded location that lies exactly on the boundary between two grid cells is moved 0.001° north or east, into one of them.
  • Tickers keep their format. The location segment (40785N73965W) is the market's point, which is no longer always a cell center.
  • Markets created before this change keep their location and stay reachable by requesting those coordinates.

item.title: Orderbook snapshots can have an empty market_id
item.description: An orderbook_snapshot for a market with no recorded change can have an empty market_id and has clock 0, whether the market was created before or after your WebSocket server started.
item.content:encoded:
An orderbook_snapshot for a market with no recorded change, such as a new market that hasn't had an order yet, can have an empty market_id, and its clock is 0. Markets created before the WebSocket server you're connected to started already worked this way. Markets created after it started used to get their UUID and creation clock instead.

Identify these markets by market_ticker. The first orderbook_delta for the market carries its market_id.

item.title: Requests with a NUL byte or invalid UTF-8 return 400
item.description: A request whose path or query string contains a NUL byte (%00) or bytes that are not valid UTF-8 now returns 400 instead of 500; a cursor carrying such text is handled as a malformed cursor.
item.content:encoded:
A request whose path or query string contains a NUL byte (%00) or bytes that are not valid UTF-8, for example GET /markets?tickers=KX%00TEST or GET /historical/trades?ticker=%ff%fe, now returns 400 invalid_parameters. It previously returned 500 internal_server_error on endpoints that looked the value up.

A cursor carrying such text is now handled the way each endpoint already handles a cursor it cannot decode, instead of returning 500. Most endpoints return 400. A few, including GET /markets, ignore a cursor they cannot decode and return the first page.

No valid request is affected, and cursors returned by the API are unchanged.

item.title: Create on-request concert markets
item.description: POST /concert_cancellation_markets returns or creates the market on whether a concert is postponed or canceled; three GET endpoints list what can be created and the concerts on offer.
item.content:encoded:
Four endpoints for on-request concert markets (series starting with KXRFQCONCERT), which pay when a show is postponed, canceled or either:

  • POST /concert_cancellation_markets returns the market for a show, its scheduled date and a cover (postponed, cancelled or either), creating it if it doesn't exist yet. created says whether it is new. Send an RFQ for the returned market_ticker with POST /communications/rfqs to trade it. A valid request that can't be offered (for example a show that has moved to another date) returns 409 concert_cancellation_market_unavailable, and reaching the creation limit returns 429 concert_cancellation_market_limit_exceeded, which is not request-rate limiting.
  • GET /concert_cancellation_markets/availability returns the covers that can be created and the metros whose concerts are listed. It needs no authentication.
  • GET /concert_cancellation_markets/concerts lists a metro's upcoming concerts, and GET /concert_cancellation_markets/concerts/search finds them by name. Both return the show id and date the create request takes.

See On-Request Concert Markets. These markets are not live yet.

item.title: Rate limit headers on REST responses
item.description: REST responses now carry X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset and X-RateLimit-Cost for the bucket each request was charged to.
item.content:encoded: REST responses now describe the rate limit bucket each request was charged to: X-RateLimit-Limit (its capacity in tokens), X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (seconds until it is full) and X-RateLimit-Cost. 429 responses carry them too, but not Retry-After. Publicly cacheable responses, which include most market data, carry none of them. See Rate limit headers.

item.title: Market expected_expiration_time is never later than latest_expiration_time
item.description: expected_expiration_time on market objects is now capped at latest_expiration_time; some markets in multi-date events previously reported a later value.
item.content:encoded: expected_expiration_time on market objects, including markets nested in events, is now capped at the market's latest_expiration_time. Some markets in events with several date strikes reported the last strike's date, which could fall after their own latest expiration. Markets whose expected expiration was already at or before the latest expiration are unchanged.

item.title: Market expiration_time removed
item.description: The deprecated expiration_time field is removed from market objects; latest_expiration_time carries the same value.
item.content:encoded: The deprecated expiration_time field is removed from market objects, including markets nested in events. Read latest_expiration_time instead: it has always carried the same value. Order expiration_time is unrelated and unchanged.

item.title: Overnight settlement price band for equities perps
item.description: Overnight, equities perps orders must be within 20% of that day's 4 PM ET settlement price; resting orders outside the band are canceled with reason SettlementBoundsCancel.
item.content:encoded: During the overnight session (8 PM to 4 AM ET), every equities perps order must be priced within 20% of the market's 4 PM ET settlement price from the day the session opened. Orders outside the band are rejected with invalid price. When the band takes effect or moves, resting orders outside it are canceled: margin user_orders and orderbook delta messages report last_update_reason: "SettlementBoundsCancel", and FIX ExecutionReports (35=8) carry a Text (58) of SETTLEMENT_BOUNDS_CANCEL. See Price Banding.

item.title: Incentive schedules, and incentive programs by series or event
item.description: GET /incentive_schedules lists the recurring incentive schedules; GET /incentive_programs takes series_ticker and event_ticker and returns each program's series and event.
item.content:encoded:
• GET /incentive_schedules lists the recurring incentive schedules that have not ended: what each market of a series (or of one event) earns per window, how long a window is, and when the schedule ends. all_markets says whether the terms are promised to every market the schedule covers, including markets listed later, or only anticipated. It needs no authentication.
  • GET /incentive_programs takes series_ticker and event_ticker filters, and each program now carries its series_ticker and event_ticker.

item.title: User hosts for fill and order updates
item.description: The lower-latency fill and user_orders hosts are now user-ws and margin-user-ws. The warp-ws and margin-warp-ws hosts are deprecated and keep working for now.
item.content:encoded:
The lower-latency hosts for fill and user_orders updates are now:

  • Production Predictions: wss://user-ws.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2
  • Production Margin: wss://margin-user-ws.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2/margin
  • Demo Predictions: wss://user-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2
  • Demo Margin: wss://margin-user-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2/margin

The user hosts serve fill and user_orders today, and more per-user channels will be added over time. See API Environments and Endpoints.

The warp-ws and margin-warp-ws hosts are deprecated. They keep working and serve the same channels for now. Move to the user hosts above.
